clue.text: Head of astrophysics acclaimed possibly in a university?

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase: belonging to or taking place in a college or university

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of astrophysics is used
possibly says the letters could be arranged some other way, so they are reshuffled

explanation.surface: An astrophysics professor has been hailed by colleagues, perhaps at their own university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges A (from 'Head of astrophysics') with ACCLAIMED.
explanation.definitionFit: Academical is an adjective for things pertaining to a college or university, such as academical dress.

clue.text: Sensitive Tory losing heart must suppress expression of pain

indicators.note: to suppress something is to hold it down within, so one piece goes inside the other
losing heart takes away the middle letters of the word Tory, leaving its ends

parts.note: ouch is what you cry when hurt

explanation.surface: A thin-skinned Conservative politician has to stifle any cry of pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing heart' leaves TY, the ends of the party word, which then holds the cry inside it ('must suppress').
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: someone easily offended or quick to take umbrage is sensitive.

clue.text: Happen to lead a board that is not invincible

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece that leads comes first, ahead of what follows

parts.note: to be is to happen or take place, as in 'so be it'
a table is a board, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: Something happens to put you ahead on a games board, showing your rival can be defeated.
explanation.definitionFit: A paraphrase: anything that can be defeated is, by definition, not invincible.

clue.text: Ferryman takes companion forward, crossing a river

indicators.note: crossing is read as straddling, so the outer pieces lie either side of the inner ones

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for Companion of Honour, a British order
on means forward, as in 'go on'
R is the standard abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: A boatman goes ahead with a friend, carrying them across the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' looks like a ferry trip, but it means the outer pair straddles the inner pair.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Charon rows the souls of the dead across the river Styx into the underworld.

clue.text: Performances around university? They have lots

indicators.note: around means the first piece is placed round the second

parts.note: actions are things performed, deeds

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about stage shows staged on a campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They have lots' plays on lots meaning plenty; in salerooms a lot is an item put up for bidding.
explanation.definitionFit: Sales by bidding offer goods in numbered lots, so these events literally have lots.

clue.text: A type of cheese not the first thing for man in garden

indicators.note: not the first thing means the opening letter of the cheese is dropped

parts.note: Edam is a round Dutch cheese

explanation.surface: A cheese-shop instruction: not that one first, and something for the gentleman in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not the first thing' drops E from EDAM, leaving DAM.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the first man lived in the Garden of Eden.

clue.text: That cut flower is something sweet

indicators.note: cut means a word has been shortened by losing its final letter

parts.note: such can mean that, as in 'such a thing' or 'that kind of thing'
a rose is a flower

explanation.surface: A cut flower from the garden is a sweet gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks SUCH to SUC; 'flower' wants to be a river here, but it is a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Sucrose is the chemical name for common table sugar, the classic sweet substance.

clue.text: Certain earth scientists sit awkwardly in various slimes and goos

indicators.note: awkwardly suggests a clumsy, jumbled arrangement, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written, part of the letters to rearrange
taken as written, part of the letters to rearrange
taken as written, part of the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Researchers squat uncomfortably amid assorted sludge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkwardly' signals the reshuffle; 'in' and 'various' read as the setting of the scene, but every letter of the three words goes into one pool.
explanation.definitionFit: These specialists study earthquakes, a branch of geophysics, so they are one kind of earth scientist.

clue.text: Daughter at back of house, underdog not half harassed

indicators.note: at back of places one piece after the others
not half means one half of the word is dropped, keeping the first four letters

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter in genealogies

explanation.surface: A girl stays behind the house while the weaker party is half-ignored and pestered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' keeps only the front half of the eight-letter word; 'at back of' sends the daughter to the very end.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to hound someone is to pursue and harass them relentlessly.

clue.text: Just unconcerned

definitions.meaning: just means fair and impartial, having no stake in the outcome
unconcerned means lacking interest, a widely used though disputed sense

explanation.surface: Simply couldn't care less.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means impartial (a just referee) and, in loose usage, simply uninterested or indifferent.

clue.text: Pointer about to be planted in country hill

indicators.note: planted in means set inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: India is a country
C is short for circa, Latin for about
a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor in south-west England

explanation.surface: A sign is about to be put up on a hill somewhere in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be planted in' puts C inside INDIA, giving INDICA.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a gauge needle or signal that shows a reading is a pointer.

clue.text: Thomas is provided with French art books

parts.note: Tom is the short form of Thomas
es is French for 'art', as in the old English 'thou art' (tu es)

explanation.surface: Thomas has been given some books on French painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'art' is not painting but the old verb form: 'thou art' is 'tu es' in French.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a tome is a book, especially a large heavy one.

clue.text: Egyptian phenomenon brings silence, then an exclamation

parts.note: mum means silent, as in 'keep mum'
'my!' is a cry of surprise

explanation.surface: Something remarkable from Egypt leaves you speechless, then makes you gasp.
explanation.definitionFit: An embalmed, wrapped body is the most famous artefact of ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Dramatist that could have nine jobs on — one must go

indicators.note: could have suggests the letters might be rearranged into something else

parts.note: taken as written: these letters, less one, are rearranged
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A playwright who might have juggled nine jobs, one of which has to be cut.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove I ('one ... must go') from the letters of NINE JOBS ON and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Ben Jonson was an English playwright, a contemporary of Shakespeare, author of Volpone.

clue.text: Each boy appears in black fur in keeping with the time

indicators.note: appears in means the pieces are placed inside the other

parts.note: sable is a black fur and the heraldic word for black
EA is the abbreviation for each, as on price tags
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: Every lad turns up wearing black fur coats, just right for winter.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraphrase: weather that suits the time of year, or a timely action, is fitting the period.

clue.text: Time to interrupt the French priest making speech?

parts.note: le is French for 'the'

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break in, so this goes into the middle of the next piece

parts.note: a curé is a French parish priest

explanation.surface: It is time to cut off the French cleric before he delivers his sermon.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a formal talk given to an audience is a speech.

clue.text: Old city slowly pressing ahead as necessary?

indicators.note: pressing ahead means this piece goes first in the down answer

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia
gently can mean slowly, with care

explanation.surface: A sleepy ancient city is moving forward bit by bit, as needed.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a loose definition: doing something as a necessity means doing it with pressing need.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something because it must be done at once is acting out of pressing necessity.

clue.text: In investigation bad person falls

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a case is a police investigation
a cad is a dishonourable man, a bounder

explanation.surface: During an inquiry, the villain takes a tumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a waterfall descending in steps, falls of water, is a cascade.

clue.text: Report of people scrutinising country residence

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: checkers are people who examine things carefully

explanation.surface: An account of inspectors at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Chequers is the British prime minister's official country house in Buckinghamshire.

clue.text: Good and exceptionally gentle, I repeatedly can be explosive

indicators.note: exceptionally hints at something out of the ordinary, so the letters are rearranged
repeatedly means the letter is used twice

explanation.surface: A kind, very mild person who, again and again, can blow up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exceptionally' rearranges GENTLE with I twice ('I repeatedly').
explanation.definitionFit: Gelignite is a blasting jelly, a high explosive used in mining and quarrying.

clue.text: Take a stand at home over little relative beginning to transgress

indicators.note: in a down answer, over means this piece sits above the next

parts.note: in means at home, as in 'staying in'
sis is short for sister

indicators.note: beginning to means only the opening letter is used

explanation.surface: At home, a parent puts their foot down over a young sibling starting to misbehave.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to stand firm or demand something firmly is to insist.

clue.text: Singer Pat offers blessing for the listener

indicators.note: for the listener means the word is taken by how it is heard

parts.note: a boon is a blessing or benefit

explanation.surface: A crooner gives a benediction to someone in the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Pat Boone is an American singer, a 1950s pop star with hits like Love Letters in the Sand.

clue.text: Secure what is embedded in seat

indicators.note: embedded in means placed inside

parts.note: to bind is to fasten or secure
'eh?' is a way of saying 'what?'

explanation.surface: Fasten whatever has got stuck in the chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seat' looks like furniture, but it is the body's seat: the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphemism: one's seat, the part one sits on, is the buttocks.

clue.text: Sarah operating in hairdressing establishment?

parts.note: Sal is a pet form of Sarah
on means operating, as in a switched-on machine

explanation.surface: Sarah is working at the hairdresser's.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair and beauty businesses are often called salons, as in a hair salon.

clue.text: Boy admitting nothing or lots?

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: a lad is a boy
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A youngster confessing to nothing or to plenty.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, a load means a great deal, as in 'loads of time'.

clue.text: Bridge opponents in the home counties

definitions.meaning: at bridge North-South play East-West, so the South and East players are on opposing sides
the home counties are the English counties surrounding London

explanation.surface: Card players facing off around London.
explanation.definitionFit: The two compass points name rival bridge seats and, joined, the region of England around London.

clue.text: Nocturnal creatures flying around the French farm buildings

indicators.note: flying around suggests letters scattered in all directions, so they are rearranged

parts.note: bats are night-flying creatures
les is the French plural for 'the'

explanation.surface: Bats swoop round the old French barns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying around' rearranges the creatures into STAB; 'around' looks like a container signal but belongs to the anagram indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Stables are buildings on a farm or estate where horses are housed.

clue.text: After row was first to become peeved

definitions.note: used as a past-tense verb: annoyed or irritated someone

indicators.note: after places one piece following the other

parts.note: a rank is a row, as of soldiers
to have led is to have been first

explanation.surface: After a quarrel, someone took the lead in getting annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' suggests a quarrel, but it is a line; 'peeved' is a verb here, meaning irritated.
explanation.definitionFit: A grievance that rankled irritated or galled someone persistently.
